root_cause.text: The mcp23s08 driver does not clear the MCP_GPINTEN register (disabling all pin interrupts) during probe, so any pre-existing interrupt-on-change configuration from a previous boot can cause the chip to generate interrupts for pins that do not yet have registered nested interrupt handlers, leading to a kernel crash when the interrupt handler tries to invoke a non-existent nested handler.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `mcp_write(mcp, MCP_GPINTEN, 0)` early in `mcp23s08_probe_one()`, and the commit message states that the bug was exposed by commit f9f4fda15e72 which made the real register value be read from the chip (instead of a default 0), and that the fix is to disable all pin interrupts during initialization.

intent_record.intent_summary: Disable all pin interrupts during probe to prevent nested handlers from being called for interrupts without actual handlers.
intent_record.what: Added a call to mcp_write(mcp, MCP_GPINTEN, 0) to disable all pin interrupts, with error handling via dev_err_probe, before setting up the gpio irq chip.
intent_record.how: At runtime, during probe, this ensures any previously enabled pin interrupts are cleared, preventing the interrupt handler from being triggered for interrupts that do not have proper handlers yet.
